seen_animation: A black-line trumpet drawn in the doodle's style (tall narrow oval bell on the left, a broken upper tube line, three or four looped valve strokes, an open zig-zag mouthpiece on the right) is held horizontally at the mouth of a grey-line man in profile facing left, in front of grey horizontal building lines and window shapes. Across frames 1-16 the trumpet stays at the mouth and makes small shifts: the bell drifts a few pixels up and down and slightly left and right, the valve loops shift along the tube, and the bell oval changes width a little (narrower in frames 10 and 14, wider in 12 and 16). There is no large change of pose; it is a sustained held note with slight sway.
seen_film: A man in a dark suit and glasses, in left-facing profile against a building facade, plays a long-bell trumpet held horizontally at his lips with both hands under the valves. Over the 16 frames he keeps playing; the horn and head make small movements: the bell end dips and rises slightly (bell a little lower in frames 3-8, a little higher and more level in frames 9-13, slightly lower again 14-16), and the head and shoulders shift a few pixels. The camera and background are steady. No other action occurs.
named_subject: A trumpet (held and played by a man in profile)
evidence: In all frames 1-16 the doodle trumpet sits where the film's trumpet sits: bell near the left edge around x=45-60 and the mouthpiece touching the grey face at the lips, matching film frames 1-16. The film's event is a steady played note with small sway, and the animation shows the same: frames 1-4 and 5-8 hold nearly identical positions with small bell drift, frames 9-13 show the horn slightly raised and shifted right as in film frames 9-13, frames 14-16 settle back. Every frame keeps the doodle's construction from c.png: tall closed oval bell, gap in the upper tube line, three-plus looped valve strokes, open angled mouthpiece. No frame shows a doubled trumpet, a missing part, or a jump in position larger than a few pixels. Judged from still frames only, not playback.
primary_gap: The trumpet's small sway is not clearly tied to the film's dip-and-rise of the bell, so the motion reads more as a slight jitter of the drawing than as the player lifting and lowering the horn.
closes_when: Across frames 3-8 the bell end sits a few pixels lower than the mouthpiece and across frames 9-13 it rises to level, with the whole trumpet rotating about the mouthpiece rather than the bell oval changing width.
protect: The doodle's exact construction and stroke habits (tall narrow oval bell, broken upper tube line, looped valve strokes, open zig-zag mouthpiece); the mouthpiece kept in contact with the grey figure's lips in every frame; the placement matching the film's trumpet; the absence of doubling or redraws.
identity_gap: The animated trumpet is the c.png drawing with its bell, broken tube line, valve loops and mouthpiece intact; only the bell oval's width varies slightly between frames, which the doodle does not call for.
